name: Amla (Phyllanthus emblica)
short: In a meta-analysis of 4 trials (227 adults with dyslipidaemia), amla fruit extract was well tolerated; adverse events were mild, mainly dyspepsia (7 events with amla). Trials lasted up to 12 weeks.
text: A meta-analysis of four randomised trials (227 adults with dyslipidaemia) of an aqueous amla fruit extract over 12 weeks found it well tolerated; adverse events reported in three of the four trials were all mild, with 7 episodes of dyspepsia in the treatment groups and diarrhoea, fever and headache in the placebo groups. In a 12-week randomised, double-blind trial in 80 people with type 2 diabetes who completed it, a standardised aqueous extract was well tolerated, without significant changes in laboratory safety parameters, and in a 12-week placebo-controlled trial in 59 people with metabolic syndrome no participant stopped because of adverse events. A review of the fruit's toxicology states that toxicological studies indicated no adverse effects even at high oral doses; the abstract does not say whether these were animal or human studies. The cited trials lasted up to 12 weeks, so they do not address longer use. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
